title: Normalized Transcript v1
description: The integration surface between Clipwise and 1on1, per Architecture Decision #12: share a format, not code. Carries the literal record only. Extraction, interpretation, and identity resolution across meetings stay on each consumer's side of the line. Adapters duplicate parser code freely; they never duplicate this contract.

contract_version.description: Bumped on any change that is not purely additive.

source.description: Source label. Consumers key deduplication on (source, source_recording_id), so this value is load-bearing: re-emitting the same recording under a changed label will duplicate rather than collide.

source_recording_id.description: The id the source uses for the recording itself. Where a source exposes several ids for one meeting, this is the one that identifies the recording, not the call, share link, or web view.

source_alt_ids.description: Any other ids the source exposes for the same meeting, keyed by kind (e.g. call_id, share_token). Present so consumers can resolve links without guessing which id is canonical.

start_time.description: ISO 8601, timezone-aware. Never a bare date.

duration_basis.description: How duration_ms was arrived at. Required to be honest rather than convenient: last_segment_start is a floor and has undershot a real call by eight minutes. A consumer that needs a true duration must check this field, not just read the number.

speakers.description: Meeting-scoped. A speaker id means nothing outside this document. Deciding that a speaker here is the same person as a speaker in another meeting is each consumer's own problem — sharing that would couple the two identity graphs, which is the coupling AD #12 exists to prevent.

display_name.description: Null where diarization failed to attach a name. Null is a per-document defect, not a normal state, but consumers must handle it.

is_recorder.description: Whether this speaker is the person who captured the meeting — the me-vs-them split that falls out of two-track capture without diarization, per AD #5. Null where the source does not expose it.

segments.description: Ordered by start_ms ascending. Overlapping segments are permitted and are common where diarization is imperfect; consumers must not assume disjoint spans.

end_ms.description: Null where the source supplies start offsets only. Deliberately not required: forcing it would make adapters synthesize an end from the next segment's start, which is a fabrication that reads as measurement.

source_url.description: Deep link into the recording at this offset, where the source provides one.

words.description: Per-word timings. Enrichment; absence is normal.

capabilities.description: What this source was able to supply. Declared rather than discovered, so a consumer degrades deliberately instead of inferring capability from nulls. A consumer that requires a capability should check here and fail loudly, not read half a transcript and proceed.

audio_url.description: Enrichment. Null for sources that do not retain audio.

source_summary.description: A summary the source generated. NOT part of the record and never a substitute for segments — source summaries have been observed to invert meaning, flattening sequencing into cancellation and delegation into decision. Carried only so a consumer can use it as a map of what to look for in the transcript. A consumer that extracts from this field rather than from segments is misusing the contract.
